html:
Barotseland is the kingdom of the Lozi people on the floodplain of the upper Zambezi in western Zambia, ruled by a king called the Litunga.

Lozi farmers built mounds above the yearly flood and drained the plain. In the 1840s the Kololo, Sotho-speaking migrants from the south, conquered them, and Sesotho words entered the Lozi language. The Lozi rose and restored their kings in 1864. The great king Lewanika signed a concession with Cecil Rhodes's company in 1890, seeking British protection.

Under British rule Barotseland kept its own king and courts. The Barotseland Agreement of 1964 joined it to independent Zambia, but the government later cancelled it, and demands for autonomy persist. The yearly Kuomboka ceremony celebrates the kingdom.
sum: Barotseland is the kingdom of the Lozi people on the floodplain of the upper Zambezi in western Zambia, ruled by a king called the Litunga.
